extracted.intended_audience: NSF staff, NSF program officers, grantees, and institutional communications/public affairs officers preparing NSF-related press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and releasing press releases about NSF-funded work, covering required wording, formatting, coordination procedures, and content-quality expectations aimed at general audiences and media outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate press release category
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify the release according to NSF categories before drafting or distributing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories listed: Budget requests and announcements; Scientific discoveries (NSF-funded research); Awards and recognitions; Research funding announcements; Major program launches; Crisis/incident communications. Select the appropriate category to determine tone, timing, and coordination needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format: AP style and federal agency style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AP style and any federal agency style requirements when preparing the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow AP style rules, federal agency style requirements, and include the standard NSF boilerplate. Ensure release conforms to governmental communications norms (e.g., attribution, capitalization, datelines) and institutional templates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard NSF boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the standard NSF boilerplate language in the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NSF's prescribed boilerplate text (institutional description and customary closing language) so releases are consistent with NSF branding and messaging. The boilerplate is part of the Format requirements and is expected on NSF-related releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Acknowledgment for NSF-Funded Research
rubrics_metrics.description: "This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant No. [Award Number]. Any opinions, findings, and conclusions or recommendations expressed in this material are those of the author(s) and do not necessarily reflect the views of the National Science Foundation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this exact acknowledgment (with the correct award number) in materials describing NSF-funded research. This is required NSF acknowledgment language for grant-funded research and must appear as stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge NSF support / clearly identify NSF as funder
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly identify NSF as the funder of the work being described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State NSF support prominently in the release (in addition to the required disclaimer). This helps ensure transparency about funding sources and informs readers and reporters of the sponsor of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use disclaimer language
rubrics_metrics.description: Include appropriate disclaimer language stating that opinions/findings are those of the authors and do not necessarily reflect NSF views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond funding attribution, ensure disclaimers (such as the required acknowledgment) are present to separate author conclusions from NSF positions. Use the exact phrasing where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with NSF program officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must coordinate announcement content with the NSF program officer responsible for the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before issuing a release about NSF-funded research, contact and coordinate with the NSF program officer to confirm factual accuracy, appropriate framing, and any additional requirements or restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination with NSF OLPA before release
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate with the NSF Office of Legislative and Public Affairs (OLPA) prior to public release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF OLPA manages press releases, media advisories, and communications about NSF-funded science; coordination enables co-promotion and ensures releases meet NSF standards and timing expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time release with publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Time the press release to coincide appropriately with publication or other external events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate the release timing with the journal publication or other milestones (e.g., embargoes) to avoid premature disclosure and to maximize accurate media coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite the journal article / peer-reviewed publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a citation to the journal article or peer-reviewed publication describing the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the full citation and, if possible, links to the paper or DOI so journalists and readers can consult the original source. This supports transparency and verifiability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain societal benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the societal benefits or broader impacts of the research in plain terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the work could affect society, technology, policy, or daily life; emphasize relevance to non-expert audiences while avoiding overclaiming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plain language for general audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Write the release in plain language accessible to a general audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid jargon, define technical terms, prioritize clarity and readability, and frame findings so non-specialists can understand significance and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include researcher contact / researcher availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide researcher contact information and make researchers available for media inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include names, affiliations, phone numbers, and email addresses for key researchers; indicate availability for interviews and provide preferred spokespeople to facilitate accurate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide multimedia
rubrics_metrics.description: Include multimedia assets (images, video, audio) to accompany the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality multimedia and captions; NSF often co-promotes multimedia, so supplying assets increases the likelihood of broader dissemination and clearer public understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish what is known vs. speculative / provide accurate scientific framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly distinguish established findings from hypotheses, speculation, or ongoing work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame results accurately, note limitations and uncertainties, avoid overstating preliminary findings, and provide context about what the research does and does not demonstrate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use sensational or exaggerated language to describe results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid clickbait phrasing and hyperbole; focus on sober, accurate representation of the science and its implications to maintain public trust and journalistic credibility.
